courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: So it's good that we can set up some global styling and some global colors but can we also say that
for example the toolbar should always have our primary background color? Now what we can do and what
I mentioned on that slide too is we can do that on a component level, so we can go to our auth page, to
the HTML file and there on the toolbar,
indeed you can set a color property
and in case you're not sure whether you can set this, you know you can go to the component docs, there
go to the toolbar section and then on ion-toolbar, you'll learn that you can set your color there, if
you scroll down you see you can set the color property. You could by the way also set the mode if you
want to overwrite that Ionic detects it automatically.
So if you want to say it should detect the mode for the entire app but for this toolbar, I actually
want to style it as if it were running on an iOS device all the time, then you could set this too but
that's not what I want to focus on,
I want to focus on the color. So we know we can set the color
and of course I can set the color here to let's say primary.
Now if we set this to primary, Ionic will behind the scenes automatically select all the right
CSS variables to color our toolbar with the primary color and please also note, to not just set that
background color to primary but it is smart enough to set the text here
to the contrast color of our primary color, the contrast color can be seen in the variables.scss file,
here is the color primary,
here is the contrast color.
So Ionic is smart enough to style everything on the toolbar, not just the background but as soon as we
login, we see that the next toolbar we see doesn't have that and this makes sense because that is that
declarative styling I mentioned on the slide, we control the look of this toolbar with the color
property or attribute but only on the auth page,
we didn't add this on our discover page.
Now obviously, you can add this to every toolbar in your application but if you know that every toolbar
should have that color, manually adding this all the time is pretty cumbersome
and thankfully, there is an easier way. If we go back to the official docs, to the guide section and then
there to theming advanced, if we scroll down a bit, you will see that there are certain application colors
you can set and these are basically CSS variables, special CSS variables Ionic will watch
out for, that are styling the important core building parts of your app, for example you could set up
your general background color which currently is white and you could set this to a different color or
your general text color. By the way for background and text, you also need to provide an RGB value because
of the way Ionic consumes and uses these colors in its components.
You can also set up a general toolbar background, a toolbar border color and a toolbar color which colors
the components in the toolbar,
so the things like the title and that looks like what we need here.
Now you can therefore go to your variables and in that root section, you could now add
--ion-toolbar-background
right,
that was this or that
is this CSS variable.
Now you can set this to any color you want,
now of course I could now set this to black or to any color I want, I can also copy that primary color
here to use my primary color
but the drawback of setting a hardcoded color here is that if I really want to use my primary color,
whenever I change my primary color up here, I will also have to change it down there and that is not
really what I want to do
and therefore instead we can simply consume our CSS variable here.
So that is the variable name and thus far, you only learned how you can set up CSS variables, like this
and by the way you don't have to set them up in the root selector,
you can set up CSS variables anywhere, the place where you set them up defines where they can be
consumed though. What you set up in root can be used anywhere in your application, in any other CSS
rule, if you set something up in let's say your own class selector, then you can only use it in that
own class selector or child elements of the element that has that class selector.
So here, this is set up in root and therefore we can use this variable anywhere
and I want to use it still in root down there
and how do you use a CSS variable?
You use the var function which is built into CSS and to var,
you pass the name of that variable and this will extract that variable value and apply it to this property
on the left, which here happens to be a variable as well
but this could also be something like the general background color, so it could be a normal CSS property
as well. The var function also takes a second argument by the way
and that would simply be a fallback value in case this variable here can't be resolved,
now we know that it will always be resolvable but you could set something like black here as a fallback
value to be super safe. So now if we save that and we have a look at our application, we see that we have
the background color but now, Ionic is not smart enough to automatically color the text as well or it's
not so much being smart or not being smart,
it's simply not the behavior Ionic wants to show,
instead these variables are there to give us fine-grained control over the look and feel of some important
Ionic parts
and if we want to change the text color or the toolbar component color as well, we have to do that with
this ion-toolbar color variable here.
So the solution is to simply set this as well
and here, the value of course should be the contrast color to our primary color.
So here, I will copy ion-color primary contrast,
so let's grab that and add it here and if we do this and we save this, we should see that our toolbar looks
exactly the way we want it to look
but now if I do login, we also see that this is the case for the other toolbars in our application and
that of course is pretty sweet because we now have a set-up that require pretty much no effort
and we now have a global styling for the toolbar or a global behavior for the toolbar with just two
lines of CSS code added. Just as a side note, what you can still do,
you can still go to a certain component,
let's say that auth page again and there, set color secondary for example on the toolbar.
Now we do have our global setup with that ion-toolbar-background and ion-toolbar-color
and yet if you set this, this will overwrite your global settings
and that's also what I talked about on the slides.
You can always overwrite the global settings,
they have the least highest priority,
so your custom CSS rules can overwrite it or these built-in attributes of certain components,
of course not just for the toolbar but also for the button and for other components. If a component
for example allows you to set a color attribute, if you set a color attribute
and this does not fit your global default, then this is fine
and this will overwrite your global default,
so you still have full control here and you can apply this in cases where you need a different look
on a single page
but want the general look on the other pages or on the other places in your app.
